observations: The runtime supplied no subagent/task identity, so task is null. I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/review/page-04.png and the text-free works/auto-6294ee8a2094/assets/panels/04-3.png with Read and looked at both. For the transitions I also opened page-03.png and page-05.png.

All lettering matches the source page 4: the three captions, the Nurse's line 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.', and the labels 'NOW · A-12' and 'RAVI · READY'. The 04-3 label text is unchanged; it is only wrapped onto two lines, 'RAVI ·' and 'READY'.

04-1: the caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' is at top-left over the window and wall. 'NOW · A-12' sits on the wall TV's screen at top-right. Ravi's face, his bag strap, his hand at his pocket and Meera at the desk are clear.

04-2: the caption 'A quick vitals check first.' is at top-left. The balloon 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' has a short tail down to the Nurse's head, above her face, which stays fully visible. Ravi's face, the cuff, the hand bulb, the monitor, the pulse oximeter and the bag on the floor are clear.
04-3: the caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' is on the plain upper wall, well clear of her face.

04-3 label, checked against the text-free art. In the art (640 px wide, page scale about 0.61), the notification card spans about panel x290-520 / y1170-1285, which is about page x786-926 / y1184-1255. The check badge and its burst sit above the card, at about page x850-885 / y1150-1195. The hand on the tablet's left edge reaches to about page x775; the hand on the right edge starts at about page x920.

In the composed page, the two-line label box sits at about page x790-918 / y1200-1307. It now falls inside the gap between the two hands. All fingers and the thumb on the left-edge hand are visible; the thumb and fingers on the right-edge hand are visible, with the label's right edge just short of them. The check badge and its burst are fully visible above the box. The round-9 defect is resolved.

Remaining overlap: the label covers the lower part of the drawn card, including its blank white strip, which is meant to be replaced by the lettering. The top band of the drawn card is still visible above and behind the box, so it reads as a stacked notification card. The box's lower edge reaches the tablet's bottom bezel and hangs a few pixels past it, covering a short stretch of the dark frame.

I judge this remaining overlap acceptable. It covers only screen UI and frame, not a face, a hand, a person or a story prop. The label clearly belongs to the tablet, under the check badge, and the alert reads instantly. It would be cosmetically cleaner if the box ended inside the screen, but this is not a defect that blocks a pass.
The trailing dot at the end of the line 'RAVI ·' reads a little unusually, but the text is unchanged and the label is easy to read as 'RAVI · READY'.

My natural scan: the 04-1 caption at top-left, across Ravi's upward gaze to the TV label at top-right; the 04-2 caption, then the Nurse's balloon below it; the 04-3 caption, then down the doctor's gaze to the tablet label. This is the script order.

There is only one spoken line, so no reply can be skipped. In each panel the caption and label read top to bottom without crossing another panel's text. The 04-2 balloon and the 04-3 caption are separated by the gutter and are at different heights, so they do not compete.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading's order and speaker match the script exactly. (1) The first reading noted that the 'RAVI · READY' box hangs a little past the tablet's bottom frame, half-covers a drawn card so that two cards stack, and breaks awkwardly after the dot. I confirm all three on the current image. The round-9 blocker, the hidden fingertips, is gone: against the text-free 04-3 art, both hands and the badge are fully visible. I judge the remaining stacked-card look and the slight bezel overhang acceptable, because they cover only screen UI and frame, and the label still reads as on the tablet. The break after the dot is a stylistic matter with the text unchanged. (2) 'NOW · A-12' sits on its monitor, which is acceptable. (3) That A-12 is Ravi's slot is supported by the third slot in 03-5, his upward look and the caption 'his slot'. (4) The place changes are carried by the captions and backgrounds. Nothing unresolved remains.
